audit.whatIsWrong: This page had Yasuo winning levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items with Skill at 1, 4-5 and 6. The already-applied mirror set the lane to Nautilus at levels 2, 3, 4-5 and 6, Skill at first item, Yasuo at 2+ items.
audit.why: The mirror is authoritative and mirror-fix.js overwrites disagreements, so five rows here were going to be flipped underneath prose that said the opposite. Nautilus's early stat check is real: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack per target, Titan's Wrath is a 12s shield, and Riptide is up every 7s at rank 1 against a 50.59% overall win rate.
audit.corrected: Proposed five paired flips (phases[N].side + win[N]) as one atomic group with matching ratings, and rewrote every line that would have contradicted the new sides: whys[1] through whys[5], phases[1].why through phases[5].why, spikes[0].text, content.early and content.mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spikes read as an unbroken Yasuo lane and never named the tools that actually carry Nautilus's early game.
audit.why: Riptide's 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s cooldown and Titan's Wrath's flat 12s are what beat Yasuo's chip before his crit item; Dredge Line's 14s at rank 1 is the punish window, not the whole matchup. The first-item and late spikes were already right and are untouched.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[0].text around Titan's Wrath, Riptide and the real 14s hook cooldown; left spikes[1..3] alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly said Wind Wall blocks the hook but never said it also blocks Depth Charge, and dosFull[1] ('Wind Wall his Q hook'), dosFull[2] ('EQ-poke him') and dontsFull[1] ('Eat his passive root chain') all carried bodies about a different subject entirely.
audit.why: Both Dredge Line and Depth Charge carry the projectile flag, and Wind Wall blocks all enemy projectiles for 4s on a 25/23/21/19/17s cooldown — so the wall answers his engage AND his ultimate, and the real decision is which one to spend it on. Riptide and Titan's Wrath are not projectiles and go through it. Sweeping Blade also cannot re-target the same enemy for a few seconds, so away from the wave you get exactly one dash on him.
audit.corrected: Rewrote report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[1].d, phases[1].why (the E lockout) and phases[4].why (hold the wall for the engage) around the two blockable projectiles and the real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named only Dredge Line and two vague self-references.
audit.why: Riptide at 7s is the cooldown that actually decides whether a trade is winnable; Dredge Line at 14s is the punish window and Depth Charge is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: All three real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: Level 2 stays yours: your dashes and Q poke beat a Dredge-Line-reliant melee.
edits.after: Level 2 is his: Titan's Wrath shields the trade and Riptide slows you out.

edits.before: Level 3 you win — Wind Wall neutralizes his only engage and you punish the cooldown.
edits.after: Level 3 is his — Riptide every 7s plus his passive root out-trades your poke.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 favour you as your mobility outclasses his and he can't stick to you.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his: he stat-checks any trade and Riptide keeps you slowed.

edits.before: Level 6 is yours: Last Breath picks a low-mobility tank whose hook is down.
edits.after: Level 6 is his: Depth Charge knocks you up and chains into the hook.

edits.before: First item you keep the edge — crit Yasuo out-damages a tank that can only body-block.
edits.after: First item is a skill fight: crit out-damages him, but a landed hook still kills you.

edits.before: E dashes through minions make you untouchable in the wave. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade cannot re-target him for a few seconds, so off the wave you get one dash. Trade only when Dredge Line is down.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Riptide is up every 7s at rank 1 and Titan's Wrath eats your burst — keep the wave near you and trade only on his cooldowns.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His window: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 but Riptide covers the gap. Farm safe, bank small leads, and never dash off the wave.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Depth Charge is a projectile — Wind Wall eats it. Hold the 25s wall for his engage, not for Riptide chip, and 6 stays survivable.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Dredge Line's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike, but he is tanky now — force only on Dredge Line's 10s cooldown.

edits.before: You out-tempo Nautilus the whole lane: his only trade tool is a slow, telegraphed Dredge Line (Q) hook, and Wind Wall eats it outright. Bait the hook, block it or dodge with Sweeping Blade, then punish the long cooldown with double-Q auto trades while he sits helpless.
edits.after: Nautilus stat-checks you here: Titan's Wrath is a 12s shield and Riptide lands every 7s at rank 1. Wind Wall eats Dredge Line (Q) outright — bait or block the hook, or sidestep it with Sweeping Blade, then punish its 14s cooldown with double-Q auto trades.

edits.before: You control levels 1-2 easily: Nautilus is a slow tank whose only threat is a single Dredge Line, and you can block it with Wind Wall or sidestep with Sweeping Blade. Punish the missed hook with double-Q trades.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 he out-stats you: his passive roots on first hit and Titan's Wrath absorbs your burst. Wind Wall blocks Dredge Line, or sidestep it with Sweeping Blade, then punish the missed hook.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 remain fully yours — his hook cooldown is long, your dash mobility is relentless, and Last Breath threatens a pick any time his Q is down. Just respect the Depth Charge knockup as a disengage on his side.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 lean to him — Riptide every 7s and Titan's Wrath beat your chip. Wind Wall blocks both Dredge Line and Depth Charge, so hold its 25s for whichever he opens with. Last Breath still needs him airborne.

edits.before: Track Nautilus's Dredge Line (Hook): Projectile — Wind Wall blocks it! When it is down — EQ-R him.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks Dredge Line AND Depth Charge — both are projectiles. Hold its 25s for his engage.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — Projectile — Wind Wall blocks it! Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1, a projectile Wind Wall blocks. - Riptide: 7s, his real lane damage. - Depth Charge: 120s and also blockable. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Dash through the wave stacking Q, tag Nautilus with Q2, and only commit the EQ3 knockup when his answer is down.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks all enemy projectiles for 4s — Dredge Line dies in it, and so does Depth Charge later.

edits.before: Nautilus wastes Dredge Line (Hook) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Punish the missed hook — 14s at rank 1 is your whole trade window.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against each target.
